Cut an Event Log into Pathways

Source: R/extract_pathways.R
extract_pathways.Rd

extract_pathways() cuts a long event log into pathways, runs of consecutive events within one unit (an actor, or an actor's session), and returns them as a data frame with one row per pathway, ready to tabulate against an outcome or to pass to a sequence model. Three cuts are available through type: each unit as one pathway, consecutive segments that each end on a terminal state, or one pathway from every occurrence of an anchor state to the next terminal state.

With terminal, the cuts keep only what reaches a terminal state: a unit without one, events after a unit's last terminal state, and anchors with no later terminal state are left out without a message, so count the units and events kept before comparing pathway frequencies across groups.

Usage

extract_pathways(
  data,
  action,
  group,
  order = NULL,
  type = c("unit", "segments", "anchored"),
  anchor = NULL,
  terminal = NULL,
  resolve = NULL,
  sep = " -> "
)

Arguments

data

A long data frame with one row per event, in time order within each unit unless order is given. A unit's rows need not be contiguous: rows of other units in between are not part of its pathways.

action

The name of the column holding each event's state.

group

The names of the columns defining the unit a pathway may not cross, typically the actor, or the actor and the session.

order

The name of a column giving the order of events within a unit; the rows are sorted by group and then by it. Default NULL, which keeps the row order.

type

The cut to make:

"unit"

(default) one pathway per unit. With terminal, each unit is cut after its last terminal state, so the pathway ends on an outcome rather than on whatever followed; units without a terminal state are left out.

"segments"

consecutive, non-overlapping pathways: each unit is cut after every terminal state, so each pathway ends on one. Events after a unit's last terminal state belong to no pathway.

"anchored"

one pathway per occurrence of anchor, closing at the first terminal state after it. Pathways may overlap, and events between a terminal state and the next anchor belong to none.

anchor

The single state that opens a pathway when type = "anchored", where it is required; the other cuts ignore it. It may also be one of the terminal states: a pathway then closes at the next terminal state after the anchor, not at the anchor itself. Default NULL.

terminal

The states that close a pathway, the closing state included. Required for "segments" and "anchored"; optional for "unit", where it cuts each unit after its last terminal state. Default NULL.

resolve

A named list that appends a resolution label as each pathway's final state. Each element is a character vector of states; a pathway takes the name of the first element whose states all occur in it, so order the list from most to least specific, and pathways matching none are labelled "Unresolved". The label becomes the last state of path, counts in length, and is the value of closes; the observed last state is kept in ends. Default NULL (no label).

sep

The separator placed between states in path. Default " -> ".

Value

A data frame with one row per pathway, in the order the pathways occur within each unit. Units appear in the order they first occur in data, or sorted by group when order is given and when type = "unit" is combined with terminal. Columns: the group columns, pathway (the pathway's number within its unit, from 1), path (the states joined with sep), length (the number of states), opens (the first state) and closes (the last state). With resolve, closes holds the resolution label and an ends column the observed last state. When no pathway is found (for example, the anchor or the terminal states never occur), an error of class nestimate_no_pathway is raised.

See also

sequence_compare, outcome_model

Examples

log <- data.frame(
  id  = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2),
  act = c("Try", "Wrong", "Hint", "Retry", "Right", "Praise",
          "Try", "Wrong", "Retry"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
# Each failure and its consequence:
extract_pathways(log, action = "act", group = "id", type = "anchored",
                 anchor = "Wrong", terminal = c("Right", "Wrong"))
#>   id pathway                            path length opens closes
#> 1  1       1 Wrong -> Hint -> Retry -> Right      4 Wrong  Right

# Each id as one episode:
extract_pathways(log, action = "act", group = "id")
#>   id pathway                                             path length opens
#> 1  1       1 Try -> Wrong -> Hint -> Retry -> Right -> Praise      6   Try
#> 2  2       1                            Try -> Wrong -> Retry      3   Try
#>   closes
#> 1 Praise
#> 2  Retry
